2026-09-12T20:15:06.7537068Z 
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7537180Z To create a pull request:
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7537497Z 1. Make any file changes directly in the working directory.
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7538358Z 2. If you haven't done so already, create a new local branch using `git checkout -b <branch-name>` with an appropriate unique name.
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7540461Z 3. Add and commit your changes to the branch. Be careful to add exactly the files you intend, and check there are no extra files left un-added. Verify you haven't deleted or changed any files you didn't intend to.
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7541374Z 4. Do not push your changes. That will be done by the tool.
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7542080Z 5. Create the pull request with the create_pull_request tool from safeoutputs exactly once, only when the final title/body/branch are ready.
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7543072Z 6. After calling `create_pull_request`, STOP. Do not probe with another PR call, do not test auth with manual `git push`, and do not rewrite git remotes.
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7543612Z

2026-09-12T20:15:06.7547211Z

2026-09-12T20:15:06.7556129Z 
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7556405Z For multiple or complex arguments, pipe a JSON object on stdin using `.` as the sentinel:
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7556840Z ```bash
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7557186Z printf '{"item_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody."}' | safeoutputs add_comment .
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7557723Z # or write to a file: safeoutputs create_pull_request . < /tmp/payload.json
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7558101Z ```
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7558205Z 
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7560177Z **Multi-line or long `body` content:** do NOT build the JSON payload with `printf`/`echo` embedding raw newlines or many escaped characters directly in the command line — the sandbox's shell command-injection guard may reject long or complex quoted arguments (reporting "expansion patterns"/"command substitution" even though none are present) and retrying the identical command will fail again. Instead, write the content to a temp file with a heredoc, then use `jq -Rs` to inject it as the `body` field:
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7561970Z ```bash
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7562191Z cat <<'EOF' > /tmp/gh-aw/body.md
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7562446Z Title
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7562557Z 
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7562672Z Multi-line body content goes here.
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7562926Z EOF
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7563404Z jq -Rs '{title: "My title", body: .}' /tmp/gh-aw/body.md | safeoutputs create_discussion .
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7563823Z ```
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7564480Z If a shell command is rejected for containing expansion patterns, do not retry the same command — switch to the heredoc + `jq -Rs` pattern above.
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7565195Z 
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7565587Z To inject an entire local file as the `body` field without re-embedding its content in the model context, use `jq -Rs`:
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7566125Z ```bash
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7566386Z jq -Rs --arg discussion_number "$DISCUSSION_NUMBER" \
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7566803Z   '{discussion_number: ($discussion_number|tonumber), body: .}' \
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7567169Z   discussion-body.md \
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7567435Z   | safeoutputs update_discussion .
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7567700Z ```
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7568503Z `jq -Rs` reads the file as a raw string (`-R`) and slurps it into a single JSON string value (`-s`), so `body` is always a valid JSON field. Piping `cat file | safeoutputs ...` does not populate `body` and will be rejected.
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7569242Z 
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7569766Z The generated command syntax above is schema-derived from each enabled tool's final `inputSchema` and is the source of truth for required/optional parameters.
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7570747Z Use `<server> --help` and `<server> <tool> --help` for the same schema-derived signatures and examples before calling any command.
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7573555Z </mcp-clis>
